thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert — gpu-node-pool-autoscale failing to add nodes (cluster: prod-inference). autoscaler errors: "unable to join nodegroup: attach role denied". queue backlog rising on /v1/generate. paged to oncall. :rotating_light:
Maria Chen: Seeing 503s on hosted-inference-prod and spikes in token queue length. Dashboard shows queue growth at 4x baseline. Sending signal to SRE channel.
Derek Patel: Acknowledged oncall. Checking cluster-autoscaler logs now.
Samir Rao: I can take lead on AWS side. Looks like nodegroup attach attempts are failing with LaunchTemplate 403 on PassRole. IAM change?
Derek Patel: cluster-autoscaler logs: "failed to launch instance: LaunchTemplate Version mismatch OR iam:PassRole denied" — full log: ```E0412 14:12:30 main.go:123] failed to scale up: error creating instance: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation. status code: 403```
Maria Chen: Customer impact: several active Hosted API requests are timing out after 10s retry window. A few Dedicated customers reported increased latency; no full downtime but degraded throughput.
Jia Lin: Noted. Posting to status page: limited degradation for inference endpoints in us-west-2. ETA unknown.
Samir Rao: On AWS console, the ASG show instances failing to attach to the nodegroup due to instance profile not being assumable by autoscaler role. Looks like an attach-policy got rolled earlier. We should try temporary mitigation: manually launch nodes with a fallback launch template that uses existing working role.
Derek Patel: Agreed. While Samir does that, I'll try to bump cluster-autoscaler to use fallback nodegroup config (max nodes +1) and relax taint checks to let pods schedule if nodes come up with different taint.
Maria Chen: Quick mitigation checklist: 1) reduce incoming concurrency for public hosted API by 30% via rate-limit, 2) route non-critical traffic to eu-west-1 region, 3) manual node spin up in us-west-2 fallback pool. Doing (1) now.
incident-bot: Oncall handoff: Derek is current oncall. Maria is coordinating mitigation. Samir taking AWS ops. 
Samir Rao: Spun up 2 fallback instances in the us-west-2 ASG using LT v-20230305 (known-good role). Instances came up but node join failed with taint mismatch: kubelet labels say node.kubernetes.io/gpu=false while pods require gpu=true. Looks like kubelet bootargs differ.
Derek Patel: Ok — plan: patch DaemonSet that applies the gpu taint/label to be tolerant for quick-scheduling, then re-label nodes to gpu=true once kubelet is confirmed. Command I'm preparing: ```kubectl label node <node-name> accelerator=gpu --overwrite && kubectl taint nodes <node-name> node-role.kubernetes.io/compute:NoSchedule-```
Maria Chen: Before removing taint, we need to ensure those nodes have GPU drivers. If not, pods will crash and increase churn. Samir, can you verify nvidia-driver status on the new instances?
Samir Rao: Verified: drivers present on one instance, other needs driver install. I can rsync the driver pkg and kick a systemd restart. Estimated ~7m.
Jia Lin: I'll adjust routing rules: divert 25% of traffic to eu-west-1 now, set rate-limit header so SDKs backoff faster. Also updating status: "Partial degradation — autoscaling in us-west-2 experiencing issues; mitigation in progress."
Derek Patel: I injected temporary tolerance into nodeSelector for the most latency-sensitive pods so they'll accept nodes without exact taint for 10m: ```kubectl patch deployment backend-gen -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/temporary-schedule":"true"}}}}}'``` This is a quick stopgap.
Maria Chen: Samir — once both nodes have drivers, can you label them and remove NoSchedule taint? We'll validate with a small canary job /v1/generate.
Samir Rao: Done for node-az2b-17: drivers ok, labeled accelerator=gpu, removed NoSchedule taint. Canaries now scheduling. node-az1a-03 still behind on install, working on rpm copy.
Derek Patel: Cluster-autoscaler logs show previous IAM error cleared for the fallback launch template. Need to open ticket to rollback attach-policy change in IAM and restore PassRole to autoscaler role. I'll create ticket after we stabilize.
Maria Chen: Status update to customers sent. Current impact: 12% of requests saw elevated latency, 0.8% error rate increase. We're rerouting and manual nodes are absorbing backlog. Keeping page open for next 30m.
incident-bot: Check-in reminder in 10m. Please ack when stable.
Jia Lin: Routing cutoff increased to 40% to speed backlog drain. Monitoring token queue; dropping slowly.
Samir Rao: node-az1a-03 now has drivers and joined, labeled. All pending GPU pods scheduled. Backlog processing at 70% of pre-incident throughput.
Derek Patel: Rolling cluster-autoscaler restart to clear stale scale-up attempts: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system``` Restart completed. Logs show normal scale-up behavior now.
Maria Chen: Confirming: queue trending down, 503s down to baseline. I'll close the page but keep follow-ups: (1) IAM policy rollback ticket, (2) add better preflight check in CI for LT role validity, (3) playbook update for taint/drivers quick-checks.
Samir Rao: Filing the IAM rollback ticket (IAM-7864) and adding notes on manual fallback LT.
Derek Patel: Filing post-incident doc. Please add timeline and impact numbers.
incident-bot: Incident thread closing in 30m if no new activity. :white_check_mark:
